newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ deposit rates likely to fall before mortgages.
newsitem.headline: NZ deposit rates likely to fall before mortgages.

text.p: New Zealand banks on Wednesday were cautious of the prospect of an immediate fall in retail lending rates after a steep drop in wholesale rates.
They said first reaction to Tuesday's 30 basis point fall in 90-day bank bills would be a cut in deposit rates. The 90-days fell another dozen points on Wednesday morning to under 9.45 percent.
Banks said their margins were very thin and the wholesale move was as yet insufficient to entice them to cut floating mortgage rates.
"I would say we would be holding off for a wee while yet," said a senior banker at one major bank who declined to be identified.
He said uncertainty about formation of a government following Saturday's inconclusive election was not the main reason why banks were holding back, but was a factor.

"Tomorrow morning the political parties may come to an agreement that the markets don't like, for all we know, and things could leap back. At the moment things are a little too uncertain to say we will drop our rates.

"There is a strong prospect we will cut our deposit rates but as for dropping mortgage rates in the next week or so, obviously we have been talking about it, but I think we will hold off for a little while yet," the banker said.
Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp's manager of personal banking, Alex Bentley, agreed the initial impact of the fall in wholesale rates would come in deposit rates.
"But over time, if the trend continues, yes, I can see some downside in mortgage rates. However, I think it is relatively early days to for anybody to be jumping in to drop rates.
"Until some clearer picture emerges on the political front, everybody is going to be a little nervous," Bentley said.

"The two days post-election have been very positive so far for the markets but it is early days and the markets might become a bit nervous if things don't start resolving themselves sooner rather than later, and when I say markets I mean possibly foreign investors might start getting a little bit jumpy if a clearer picture doesn't emerge in the next fortnight."
A spokesman at Westpac Bank said that at the moment it would hold off dropping its rates.

Bentley said mortgages would fall if the political environment started to clarify and there was an explicit statement from the Reserve Bank saying there was room for an easing of monetary policy if the trend down in inflation pressures continued.
Paul Hale, Treasurer at Countrywide Bank, agreed it may take a signal from the Reserve Bank for retail rates to fall.
"Only when the RB sanctions a fall in interest rates will the banks pass it through to customers and we will see a fall in retail interest rates."

Hale said that if wholesale rates sustained their lower levels, then competitive pressure in the banking market would force banks to move. But he described Tuesday's fall as a "blip" and 90-days had been hovering around 10 percent for months.
"One swallow does not make a summer," he said.
